items.documentText:
# Comparison Analysis V2 Prompt Snapshot

Use this analysis framing in V2:

- For topic mode: compare retrieved evidence for the user prompt and call out meaningful differences with citations.
- For comprehensive mode: align sections semantically (not by numbering), summarize high-impact differences, and include explicit count metrics.
- Always include practical implications and next-step recommendations.
- Keep citations in `[file:page]` format where available.

items.title: comparison-format-v2.md
items.documentText:
# Comparison Response Format V2

## Comprehensive Comparison

1. Question and compared documents.
   - Use `Source Document` (first selected in UI) and `Target Document` (second selected in UI).
2. Count summary:
   - Source topics total
   - Target topics total
   - Matching topics
   - Source not in target
   - Target not in source
   - Count validation pass/fail
3. `### Comparison Analysis` narrative (executive summary, risks, practical actions).
4. `### Alignment Summary` with balance checks and matched-topic count.
5. Matching topics list with citations.
6. Source-only topics with citations.
7. Target-only topics with citations.

## Topic Comparison

1. Question and compared documents.
   - Use `Source Document` (first selected in UI) and `Target Document` (second selected in UI).
2. Evidence count per document.
3. `### Comparison Analysis` section.
4. `### Comparative Assessment` section:
   - Key similarities
   - Key differences
   - Missing evidence caveats
   - If model analysis is sparse, provide deterministic fallback assessment from retrieved evidence.
5. `### Alignment Summary` (evidence count and assessment status).
6. Evidence lists for source and target documents.

Cross-cutting:
- Inline citations in `[file:page]` format should be hyperlinkable to the corresponding document/page when document URL is available.

# Comparison V2 Config Manifest

Source of truth reviewed: `app/services/langgraphs/compliance/complianceComparisonService2.js`

## Scope
- This manifest inventories runtime knobs used by `complianceComparisonGraphV2`.
- Goal: identify all configuration points before externalizing to files and then GeisingerConfig.
- Status labels: `env-configurable`, `hard-coded`, `partially-configurable`.

## Already Env-Configurable
- `GEISINGER_PREPARATION_VERSION` | Used for prep-version guardrail. | Status: `env-configurable`
- `COMPLIANCE_COMPARISON_MAX_SECTIONS_PER_DOCUMENT` | Caps comprehensive extracted sections per doc. | Status: `env-configurable`
- `COMPLIANCE_COMPARISON_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD` | Candidate edge threshold. | Status: `env-configurable`
- `COMPLIANCE_COMPARISON_AUTO_MATCH_THRESHOLD` | Global one-to-one auto match threshold. | Status: `env-configurable`
- `COMPLIANCE_COMPARISON_LLM_ADJUDICATION_THRESHOLD` | LLM adjudication threshold for primary pass. | Status: `env-configurable`
- `COMPLIANCE_COMPARISON_SECONDARY_MATCH_THRESHOLD` | Secondary many-to-one threshold. | Status: `env-configurable`
- `COMPLIANCE_COMPARISON_DEBUG` | Debug JSONL on/off. | Status: `env-configurable`
- `COMPLIANCE_COMPARISON_DEBUG_PATH` | Debug JSONL path. | Status: `env-configurable`
- `COMPLIANCE_COMPARISON_DEBUG_INCLUDE_FULL_CONTENT` | Include full section content in debug payload. | Status: `env-configurable`
- `COMPLIANCE_COMPARISON_MARKDOWN_LIST_LIMIT` | Render cap for markdown lists. | Status: `env-configurable`

## Core Config Object: Mode
- `mode.comprehensiveKeywords` default list (`whole document`, `full comparison`, etc.) | Source: hard-coded object. | Status: `hard-coded`

## Core Config Object: Retrieval
- `retrieval.searchFields` default `['content', 'title', 'smart_file_name']` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `retrieval.selectFields` default `['id','smartnote_id','smart_file_name','title','content','page','createdAt']` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `retrieval.topicMode.keywordTop` default `70` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `retrieval.topicMode.semanticTop` default `70` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `retrieval.topicMode.maxVariants` default `4` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `retrieval.topicMode.maxCandidatesAfterMerge` default `220` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `retrieval.topicMode.evidencePerDocument` default `16` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `retrieval.comprehensiveMode.maxSectionsPerDocument` default dynamic from env helper, fallback `220` | Status: `partially-configurable`
- `retrieval.comprehensiveMode.chunkFetchTop` default `1200` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `retrieval.comprehensiveMode.minTitleLength` default `2` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `retrieval.comprehensiveMode.minContentLength` default `20` | Status: `hard-coded`

## Core Config Object: Ranking
- `ranking.scoreWeight` default `1` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `ranking.exactSectionBoost` default `3.5` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `ranking.titleTermBoost` default `1.2` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `ranking.contentTermBoost` default `0.4` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `ranking.exactPromptBoost` default `2` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `ranking.variantBoost.exact` default `0.8` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `ranking.variantBoost.normalized` default `0.5` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `ranking.variantBoost.sectionOnly` default `0.7` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `ranking.variantBoost.quotedClause` default `0.3` | Status: `hard-coded`

## Core Config Object: Alignment
- `alignment.similarityThreshold` default `0.55` with env override | Status: `partially-configurable`
- `alignment.autoMatchThreshold` default `0.86` with env override | Status: `partially-configurable`
- `alignment.llmAdjudicationThreshold` default `0.72` with env override | Status: `partially-configurable`
- `alignment.secondaryMatchThreshold` default `0.88` with env override | Status: `partially-configurable`
- `alignment.maxTargetCandidatesPerSource` default `4` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `alignment.fallbackSearch.enabled` default `true` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `alignment.fallbackSearch.onlyWhenNoPrimaryCandidate` default `true` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `alignment.fallbackSearch.maxVariants` default `2` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `alignment.fallbackSearch.keywordTop` default `18` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `alignment.fallbackSearch.semanticTop` default `18` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `alignment.fallbackSearch.maxCandidatesAfterMerge` default `32` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `alignment.fallbackSearch.maxTargetCandidatesPerSource` default `3` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `alignment.fallbackSearch.autoMatchThreshold` default `0.9` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `alignment.fallbackSearch.llmAdjudicationThreshold` default `0.6` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `alignment.fallbackSearch.maxSourceOnlyTopicsToProbe` default `20` | Status: `hard-coded`

## Core Config Object: Completion
- `completion.preferredModels` default `['openai-5.1','gpt-4o']` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `completion.temperature` default `0.2` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `completion.maxTokens` default `1400` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `completion.maxShortTokens` default `800` | Status: `hard-coded`

## Additional Runtime Constants Outside Core Config
- `SEARCH_INDEX_NAME` default `'geisinger-002'` | Status: `hard-coded`
- `GEISINGER_COLLECTION` default `'user_collection'` | Status: `hard-coded`
- Embedding model in batch embeddings: `'text-embedding-ada-002'` | Status: `hard-coded`
- Embeddings client deployment: `'gpt-4o-aisvc'` | Status: `hard-coded`
- Embeddings client API version: `'2023-05-15'` | Status: `hard-coded`
- Progress heartbeat interval default `8000ms` | Status: `hard-coded`
- Heartbeat stage messages array | Status: `hard-coded`
- Spreadsheet upload container `'compliance-ai'` | Status: `hard-coded`
- Spreadsheet path prefix `'document-comparisons'` | Status: `hard-coded`
- Spreadsheet file pattern `'comparison-v2-{timestamp}.xlsx'` | Status: `hard-coded`
- SharePoint host switch from `USE_VAULT` (`geisinger.sharepoint.com` vs `sp-cloud.kp.org`) | Status: `env-configurable` via `USE_VAULT`

## Additional Hard-Coded Fallback Defaults Used In Logic
- `callCompletionWithFallback` fallback max tokens `1200` when config missing | Status: `hard-coded fallback`
- `callCompletionWithFallback` fallback model `gpt-4o` when preferred models missing | Status: `hard-coded fallback`
- `runFallbackSearchForConversationSection` defaults when fallback config absent:
- `maxVariants=4`, `keywordTop=35`, `semanticTop=35`, `maxCandidatesAfterMerge=70` | Status: `hard-coded fallback`
- Fallback ranking shortlist default `maxTargetCandidatesPerSource=6` | Status: `hard-coded fallback`
- Fallback similarity defaults `autoMatchThreshold=0.9`, `llmAdjudicationThreshold=0.6` | Status: `hard-coded fallback`

## Formatting And Prompt-Surface Constants
- Topic-mode evidence display cap `10` per side in markdown | Status: `hard-coded`
- LLM analysis payload preview caps in comprehensive analysis (`matched/sourceOnly/targetOnly` capped to `20`) | Status: `hard-coded`
- Several prompt strings are inline in code:
- Topic comparison system and user instructions
- Comprehensive analysis system and user instructions
- Adjudication system and user instructions
- Difference assessment fallback prose
- These are not currently file-backed in V2 | Status: `hard-coded`

## Existing Config Assets Not Consumed By V2
- `app/services/langgraphs/compliance/config/comparison-retrieval-v2.json`
- `app/services/langgraphs/compliance/config/comparison-alignment-v2.json`
- `app/services/langgraphs/compliance/config/comparison-analysis-v2.md`
- `app/services/langgraphs/compliance/config/comparison-format-v2.md`
- V2 currently loads `HARD_CODED_COMPARISON_CONFIG` directly and does not read these files.

## Proposed Externalization Targets (Phase 1: File-Backed)
- `config/comparison-mode-v2.json` for mode keyword detection.
- `config/comparison-retrieval-v2.json` for retrieval knobs.
- `config/comparison-ranking-v2.json` for ranking weights.
- `config/comparison-alignment-v2.json` for primary/secondary/fallback matching knobs.
- `config/comparison-completion-v2.json` for model and token controls.
- `config/comparison-runtime-v2.json` for index, collection, heartbeat, artifact naming/path/container.
- `config/comparison-prompts-v2.md` or split prompt files for topic/comprehensive/adjudication text.

## Proposed Externalization Targets (Phase 2: Geisinger Config Runtime)
- Persist same schema payloads as GeisingerConfig documents under a dedicated comparison collection.
- Use file values as defaults when Geisinger docs are absent.
- Add optional refresh/caching behavior so changes apply without rebuild.

## Completeness Statement
- Based on code scan of `complianceComparisonService2.js`, this manifest captures all primary config paths and major runtime literals that influence behavior, quality, and output volume.
- Before implementation, we should decide whether to externalize prompt prose and artifact naming in the same pass or defer those to a second pass.

items.title: comparison-v2-externalization-checklist.md
items.documentText:
# Comparison V2 Externalization Checklist

Companion to: `app/services/langgraphs/compliance/config/comparison-v2-config-manifest.md`

## Objective
Externalize all V2 comparison behavior controls from `complianceComparisonService2.js` to config files first, then to GeisingerConfig runtime documents, without changing current behavior by default.

## Success Criteria
- No functional regression in topic/comprehensive modes.
- Existing env overrides keep working.
- Defaults remain backward-compatible when no external config is present.
- Config can be changed without rebuild in Phase 2.

## Non-Goals (For This Plan)
- Rewriting comparison algorithm semantics.
- Migrating legacy `complianceComparisonService.js` behavior.
- UI redesign or progress UX changes.

## Precedence Contract
Use this precedence order for every config key:
1. GeisingerConfig runtime value (Phase 2)
2. Local file config value (Phase 1)
3. Env override (where intentionally supported)
4. Hard-coded safe default

Note:
- For keys already env-driven in production workflows, keep env as a supported override; do not remove unless explicitly approved.

## PR Plan

### PR1: Config Loader Foundation (No Behavior Change)
- Add `app/services/langgraphs/compliance/config/loadComparisonConfigV2.js`.
- Implement typed merge of config fragments:
- `comparison-mode-v2.json`
- `comparison-retrieval-v2.json`
- `comparison-ranking-v2.json`
- `comparison-alignment-v2.json`
- `comparison-completion-v2.json`
- `comparison-runtime-v2.json`
- Implement schema validation and coercion:
- Numeric bounds for thresholds (`0..1`) and token limits (`>0`).
- Required arrays (`searchFields`, `selectFields`, model list).
- Boolean normalization for feature flags.
- Add unit tests for loader merge behavior.
- Add unit tests for invalid file values and fallback behavior.

Acceptance checks:
- Loader returns a complete config object matching current defaults.
- Invalid file values do not crash runtime; they fall back safely.

### PR2: Wire V2 Service To Loader (No Semantic Change)
- Replace `HARD_CODED_COMPARISON_CONFIG` construction with loader output in `loadConfigNodeV2`.
- Preserve all current defaults exactly in config files.
- Keep all existing env overrides active and applied after file load.
- Add startup/config snapshot logging (non-sensitive) with kpmsg name like `comparisonV2ConfigResolved`.

Acceptance checks:
- Before/after run on same input yields equivalent counts and mode routing.
- No compile/lint errors.

### PR3: Externalize Prompt Surface
- Move inline prompt text to file-backed prompt config:
- Topic analysis system/user instructions.
- Comprehensive analysis system/user instructions.
- Adjudication system/user instructions.
- Optional fallback narrative templates.
- Add safe defaults in code if prompt files missing.

Acceptance checks:
- Prompts resolve from files when present.
- Missing prompt files do not break execution.

### PR4: Externalize Runtime Constants
- Move these to `comparison-runtime-v2.json` with defaults:
- `search.indexName`
- `data.collectionName`
- `heartbeat.intervalMs`
- `heartbeat.stages[]`
- `artifact.containerName`
- `artifact.pathPrefix`
- `artifact.filePattern`
- Keep sensitive values in env only; runtime file stores non-secret knobs.

Acceptance checks:
- Spreadsheet and progress behavior remain functional.
- Search and DB reads still target expected resources.

### PR5: GeisingerConfig Runtime Overlay (No-Build Updates)
- Add query/parse layer for comparison config docs (new collection name recommended: `Document Comparison V2 Config`).
- Resolve runtime config by precedence contract.
- Add in-memory cache with TTL (for example 60s) and cache-bypass flag for troubleshooting.
- Add failure-safe path: if DB config unavailable/invalid, continue with file/env/default chain.

Acceptance checks:
- Updating GeisingerConfig changes behavior without rebuild/redeploy.
- If DB unavailable, service still runs with file/env/defaults.

### PR6: Admin/Operational Guardrails
- Add validation endpoint or admin utility to preview effective config and source-by-key.
- Add audit-safe logs for config version/hash and source (db/file/env/default).
- Add runbook docs for rollback:
- Disable DB overlay.
- Revert to file/env.
- Revert env thresholds.

Acceptance checks:
- Operators can identify active values and sources quickly.
- Rollback path is documented and tested.

## Key Schema Proposal

### comparison-mode-v2.json
- `comprehensiveKeywords: string[]`

### comparison-retrieval-v2.json
- `searchFields: string[]`
- `selectFields: string[]`
- `topicMode.keywordTop: number`
- `topicMode.semanticTop: number`
- `topicMode.maxVariants: number`
- `topicMode.maxCandidatesAfterMerge: number`
- `topicMode.evidencePerDocument: number`
- `comprehensiveMode.maxSectionsPerDocument: number`
- `comprehensiveMode.chunkFetchTop: number`
- `comprehensiveMode.minTitleLength: number`
- `comprehensiveMode.minContentLength: number`

### comparison-ranking-v2.json
- `scoreWeight: number`
- `exactSectionBoost: number`
- `titleTermBoost: number`
- `contentTermBoost: number`
- `exactPromptBoost: number`
- `variantBoost.exact: number`
- `variantBoost.normalized: number`
- `variantBoost.sectionOnly: number`
- `variantBoost.quotedClause: number`

### comparison-alignment-v2.json
- `similarityThreshold: number`
- `autoMatchThreshold: number`
- `llmAdjudicationThreshold: number`
- `secondaryMatchThreshold: number`
- `maxTargetCandidatesPerSource: number`
- `fallbackSearch.enabled: boolean`
- `fallbackSearch.onlyWhenNoPrimaryCandidate: boolean`
- `fallbackSearch.maxVariants: number`
- `fallbackSearch.keywordTop: number`
- `fallbackSearch.semanticTop: number`
- `fallbackSearch.maxCandidatesAfterMerge: number`
- `fallbackSearch.maxTargetCandidatesPerSource: number`
- `fallbackSearch.autoMatchThreshold: number`
- `fallbackSearch.llmAdjudicationThreshold: number`
- `fallbackSearch.maxSourceOnlyTopicsToProbe: number`

### comparison-completion-v2.json
- `preferredModels: string[]`
- `temperature: number`
- `maxTokens: number`
- `maxShortTokens: number`

### comparison-runtime-v2.json
- `search.indexName: string`
- `data.collectionName: string`
- `embedding.model: string`
- `embedding.deployment: string`
- `embedding.apiVersion: string`
- `heartbeat.intervalMs: number`
- `heartbeat.stages: string[]`
- `artifact.containerName: string`
- `artifact.pathPrefix: string`
- `artifact.filePattern: string`
- `display.topicEvidenceLimit: number`
- `display.analysisPreviewLimit: number`

## Test Plan (Per PR)
- Snapshot tests for resolved config object.
- Regression run with fixed documents and prompt:
- Compare counts (`matching`, `sourceOnly`, `targetOnly`, `primary`, `secondary`, `fallbackRecovered`).
- Compare validation flags (`sourceBalanced`, `targetBalanced`).
- Compare runtime duration budget.
- Negative tests:
- Missing config files.
- Malformed numeric values.
- Out-of-range thresholds.
- Missing GeisingerConfig docs.

## Rollout Strategy
- Stage 1: Merge PR1-PR2 behind default-off flag for loader use.
- Stage 2: Enable loader in dev; compare output parity over multiple runs.
- Stage 3: Merge PR3-PR4 and validate output quality unchanged.
- Stage 4: Introduce PR5 overlay in dev only, then uat.
- Stage 5: Promote to prod with canary and rapid rollback switch.

## Risk Register
- Risk: config drift between files and DB docs.
- Mitigation: config hash logging and source-by-key diagnostics.
- Risk: malformed config causes runtime failures.
- Mitigation: strict validation and fallback chain.
- Risk: unexpected quality shift after threshold edits.
- Mitigation: guarded rollout with baseline comparison job.
- Risk: operator confusion on active config source.
- Mitigation: effective config endpoint/report.

## Open Decisions Before Implementation
- Whether env overrides remain highest priority for specific keys.
- Whether prompt text externalization is included in first coding pass.
- Cache TTL and refresh semantics for GeisingerConfig overlay.
- Whether to externalize artifact naming/container now or later.

items.title: conversation-answer-v2.md
items.documentText:
# Conversation Answer V2

System prompt:

You are a healthcare compliance analyst. Answer only from provided evidence snippets.
If evidence is insufficient, say so explicitly and list what is missing.
Always cite evidence as [file:page].

Generation settings:
- model: gpt-4o
- temperature: 0.2
- max_completion_tokens: 1200

Answer requirements:
1. Provide a direct answer first.
2. Include key supporting points with citations.
3. If unsupported, state limitations and what evidence would resolve uncertainty.

items.title: conversation-format-v2.md
items.documentText:
# Conversation Format V2

Primary response template (aligned to legacy behavior):

```md
## Document Overview

**Document:** ${documentDisplay}

---

**Your Question:**
_${userPrompt}_

---

**What I found:**

${conversationResponse}
```

Notes:
- For selected-document mode, `documentDisplay` should be `[${fileAName}](${url})`.
- For all-docs-in-LOB mode, append `### Documents Used` after the template.
- For all-docs-in-LOB mode, `documentDisplay` should be plain text (no hyperlink).
- `url` should include `?target=_blank` and append `#page=<top evidence page>` when available.
- Inline citations like `[file:page]` should be linkified to the corresponding `url#page=<page>` when a document URL is available.
- Evidence snippets are not shown by default in final markdown.

items.documentText:
# Initial Intent Config V2

This file is the external snapshot of the runtime hardcoded config used by Compliance AI2 initial intent flow.

Supported lines of business:
- Medicare
- Medicaid
- CHIP
- Commercial
- Marketplace
- NCQA

Behavior:
- Primary audience is LOB compliance officers; default framing should be regulatory/compliance-focused.
- Prefer language around policy requirements, controls, audits, implementation obligations, and compliance risk.
- Avoid member/citizen-support framing unless user explicitly asks from that perspective.
- LOB intent should be inferred using concept-level distinctions and PA context, not only keyword matching.
- LOB reference anchors used for intent grounding:
  - CHIP: https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dhs/resources/chip
  - Marketplace (Pennie): https://pennie.com/
  - Medicare: https://www.pa.gov/agencies/aging/aging-programs-and-services/pa-medi-medicare-counseling
  - Medicaid: https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dhs/resources/medicaid
  - Commercial: https://www.geisinger.org/health-plan/employers/small-business
  - NCQA: https://healthinsuranceratings.ncqa.org/2019/search/Commercial/PA
- Interaction intent is two-stage after LOB inference:
  - `Comparison` only when explicit compare intent is present (compare/versus/vs/differences/side-by-side/contrast/between two options).
  - Otherwise default to `Conversation`.
- If user prompt is outside supported lines of business, return exactly:
  `I'm happy to answer questions related to the following lines of business: Medicare, Medicaid, CHIP, Commercial, Marketplace, NCQA.`
- Normalize `ACA` to `Marketplace`.
- Do not include SharePoint guidance or links.
- Document preparation is handled by admin workflows.

Runtime source:
- `app/services/langgraphs/compliance/initialIntentConfig.js`

Documents included in runtime config:
1. Background prompt (`purpose=Background`)
2. User intent schema prompt (`purpose=UserIntent`, title `Initial User Intent`)
3. Chat completion config (`purpose=ChatCompletionConfig`, title `Initial User Intent Chat Completion Config`)
4. Response format (`purpose=FormatConfig`, title `Initial User Intent Format Response`)
